commonPoints: The viewfinder should reach eye level (Ulanzi, ProMediaGear)
A travel tripod trades height for packed size (Ulanzi, Vanguard)
The center column adds height but costs stability (DPReview threads)
A 6 ft person needs roughly 60 in without the column (Ulanzi)

ourGain.point: Column-down height of five real travel tripods against a 6 ft target of 60-62 in legs only: Vanguard VEO 3T 265HCP 48.7 in, Befree Advanced 50.39 in, Peak Design Travel 51.25 in, Pro 54.3 in, Pro Tall 63.8 in; only the Pro Tall closes the gap.
'Extended height' travel tripods get it from the column: the VEO 3T 265HCP's 64.4 in max is 15.7 in above its 48.7 in legs-only height, and the Befree Advanced stays below 60 in even fully raised.

Rule by inches short with the column down: up to about 6 in = raise the column on calm days; 6-10 in = a mid-size 4-section tripod folding about 20 in; 10+ in = tall legs folding about 23 in, checked or carried diagonally.
ourGain.source: own calculation from the spec table and the pillar's eye-level rule

ourGain.point: Carry-on limit 22 x 14 x 9 in (Delta): the 22.9 in Pro Tall is longer than the bag; the 19.7 in Pro fits lengthwise.
